In reply to Thierry Abalea (Shipfox)'s message:
Interesting study, and I do agree that AI-assisted productivity is often overhyped. But I think there’s a big methodological bias in how the study was set up. They say they randomly assigned each issue to either allow or disallow AI usage, but that’s not how developers work in real life.

In practice, developers choose when to use AI and when not to. Some tasks are better suited to AI assistance, like boilerplate, repetitive code, or basic integration. Others require deep context or architectural thinking where AI may actually slow things down. Random assignment ignores that nuance.

I assume the researchers did it this way to prevent developers from picking only easy tasks for AI, which makes sense. But a more realistic approach could be to let developers identify which issues they believe AI would help with, then randomly split that subset into two groups: AI allowed and AI not allowed. That would better reflect how developers actually use these tools in real-world scenarios.
